mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a bump-out addition and a full bedroom addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bump-out extends an existing wall outward by a few feet, creating extra room for a larger closet, sitting area, or bed alcove without pouring a full-scale separate foundation footprint. A full bedroom addition builds an entirely new enclosed room from the ground up, requiring its own foundation, exterior walls, and roof tie-in. While a bump-out involves lower material costs and quicker framing, a full addition adds significantly more square footage and allows for separate private living suites or attached bathrooms.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bump-out expands an existing room by a few feet, while a full bedroom addition builds an entirely new enclosed living space from a new foundation up to the roof.
